subject: Private patch release: slice-based snapshot & reversion protocol
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: maria.gonzalez@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short maintenance window for security micropatching

Marissa —

We have a security bulletin requiring a micropatch to the Private control-plane connector next week. Can Redwood schedule a short maintenance window (ideally a 45–90 minute window) for our VPC deployment? We need:
- a guaranteed snapshot of customer KV and model pin metadata before change
- a staged canary for 5% of traffic (non-prod routing)
- a tested reversion procedure that does not require DB restore (prefer in-place reversion)

We're OK with a late-evening Monday or early-Sunday morning UTC. Please advise your preferred slot and what evidence you can provide post-op (audit log, kernel/agent version report).

Thanks,
James Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Health

Attachment: 20261001-acme-schedule-proposal.pdf (pdf, 72KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: James Park <james.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short maintenance window for security micropatching

James —

Thanks for the heads up. We're aligned on the requirements. High level plan (candidate window: Mon 2026-10-05 02:00–03:30 UTC):

1) Pre-op (T-120 to T-30):
   - take immutable snapshot of KV and pin metadata (snapshot id stamped to ticket).
   - export model-config.json and a git-tagged release for the agent.
   - run a quick smoke test on a staging clone.

2) Canary (T-30 to T+20):
   - roll the agent to a 5% canary in a fenced network slice (non-customer traffic) using our routing policy.
   - telemetry gate (latency, error-rate, token-failure) 30m.

3) Release slice (T+20 to T+80):
   - progressive 25% -> 50% -> 100% for customer-facing control-plane components, with 10m hold between jumps.

4) Reversion (fast path):
   - if telemetry gate trips, we will execute a binary-level reversion that flips to the previously git-tagged agent and restores the in-memory pin table snapshot via our snapshot apply tool (no DB full restore).
   - fallback: DB restore from snapshot and full config reconcile (long path).

Deliverables after window: audit log bundle, agent version manifest, snapshot checksum, and per-route perf summary.

I'll coordinate the final runbook with Neha and Soojin and share a concise checklist by tomorrow EOD. Does Monday 02:00–03:30 UTC work for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: snapshot-checklist-v1.md (text, 3KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, James Park <james.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short maintenance window for security micropatching

Looping in the ops runbook details so we have a single source of truth. Key operational notes (from the on-call runbook):

- Snapshot fencing: use snapshot-store:/acme/kv/20261001-<random> with checksum. Snapshot apply is idempotent and supports partial ranges — we'll snapshot only service-scoped keys to minimize restore surface.
- Canary traffic shaping: create a routing-tag "acme-canary-5pct" and verify NAT/egress policies are isolated (Maria, confirm your routing table allows the canary slice).
- Telemetry gates (thresholds):
   * 99th pct latency increase > 20% OR
   * request error-rate > 0.8% OR
   * token failure increase > 0.2%
  Any single gate trip triggers fast-path reversion.
- Fast-path reversion checklist (3 steps):
   1) flip agent symlink to previous git tag (0.41.2 -> 0.40.9).
   2) apply snapshot delta: snapshot-apply --id=20261001-XXX --range=services
   3) restart agent in fenced slice with zero-downtime toggle.

I'll draft the exact CLI commands and confirm runbook ownership. Marissa — can you add a short acceptance test (curl + token check) to the runbook for the post-apply smoke?

-Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

All good from Acme Health side — Monday 2026-10-05 02:00–03:30 UTC is approved. A couple of small asks before you run:

1) Please share the pre-op snapshot ID and the post-op audit bundle to our shared Drive link.
2) During the canary, tag the traces with request.header.x-acme-canary so we can filter in our SRE dashboards.
3) If you end up on the long-path DB restore, please escalate to my pager immediately so we can pause downstream jobs.

Appreciate the clear plan — we will monitor and stand by for the final runbook.

Thanks,
James
